back_answer: A company that owns or controls production facilities for goods or services in more than one country.

front_question: How do MNCs interlink production across different countries?
back_answer: MNCs interlink production by establishing joint ventures with local firms, acquiring local domestic enterprises (e.g. Cargill buying Parakh Foods), placing sub-contracting orders with small producers, and deploying global supply chains.

front_question: What key technological innovations accelerated the pace of globalisation in logistics and communication?
back_answer: Containerization (standardized sea/rail containers cutting port handling time and transport cost) and Information & Communication Technology (satellite communication, internet, digital file transfer for service exports).

front_question: What is Liberalisation, and when did India adopt major trade liberalisation policies?
back_answer: Liberalisation is the removal of government restrictions, import tariffs, and trade barriers. India implemented major liberalisation reforms in 1991.

front_question: What role does the World Trade Organisation (WTO) play, and what is a primary criticism of its operations?
back_answer: The WTO establishes rules for global free trade. A major criticism is that developed nations force developing nations to eliminate trade barriers while retaining massive domestic agricultural subsidies themselves.

front_question: Why has the impact of globalisation been uneven across different socio-economic groups in India?
back_answer: Benefited urban wealthy consumers (greater choice, lower prices), large Indian MNCs (Infosys, Tata), and IT professionals, but severely damaged small domestic manufacturers (capacitors, toys shutting down) and forced workers into flexible, insecure unorganized employment.

front_question: What are Special Economic Zones (SEZs), and why are they created?
back_answer: Designated industrial zones with world-class infrastructure, 5-year tax holidays, and flexible labor laws established by governments to attract foreign direct investment (FDI).
